page.layout: Single printed page, one column. Running head at top with page number 628 at left. Four lines of Arabic verse at the top of the column, then a sixth Arabic line with a ornament, which leads into Latin text in italic and roman type with side-notes at the right. The Latin text runs down to the bottom of the column. The right edge of the scan cuts off the ends of several lines. No catchword, no signature, no margin notes readable as text.

main_text.p: عند ذلك ثبتوا اهل جبل لبنان وحمص وحماه وحلب علي المغالة [?] المقدم ذكرهما وعلي واب [?] الجامع المقدسة وانتسبوا باجبعهم الي دير مارون وسيبوا [?] موارنة علي اسم الدير ۞ Tune per-manserunt incolæ Montis Libani & Hemes Hemat, & Aleppi in memorata jam sententia, & in decretis seu mente Sanctorum Conciliorum, ac relati sunt omnes ad Monasterium Maronis, ac nominati sunt Maronitæ de nomine Monasterii. Et hæ[?] paucis de Maronibus, & Maronitis, e[?] quibus planissimè patescit, quàm frivol[?] sunt, quæ de illis nonnulli scripserunt.
II. Quæris quo argumento probo Joa-nem Episcopum Darensem Syrum, cu[?]mentio fit in meis notis pag. 131. & ali-[?] claruisse seculo quarto & Commentar[?] in libros D. Dionysii de utraque Hie-

page.notes: Right edge of the scan is cropped, so the last letters of several lines are missing or cut (e.g. "ad", "sunt", "e", "frivol", "Hæ", "Commentar", "ali", "cu", "Hie"); these are marked [?] and not completed. Arabic lines are written from a low-resolution image; uncertain words are marked [?]. A small "4" mark stands in the right margin beside the second Arabic line, and an ornament ۞ follows the sixth Arabic line; both are printed signs, not text. The Latin word "Hemes" and the "Hemat" are as far as the scan allows to be read. Short tick marks and specks in the margins are not printed text. The first Arabic line may continue from the previous page, so the paragraph is marked cont="true".
